questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience living outside of Europe and the US. and I wanted to get new perspectives on social science. Another import aspect for choosing Japan, is that the country is known for its technological innovations. As a Social Data Scientist, it was interesting to dive into this area and explore how digital designs are interwoven in Japanese society like for example digital art, games, transportation, contactless dining via robot waiters and autonomous security robots patrolling in the airport. Another thing that made me chose Japan is that the country is culturally rich and has beautiful nature for hiking in my spare time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Because of COVID the university was very late in giving me the information I needed and the Japanese Embassy was late as well because many was applying for a VISA now that the country had reopened. However, in the end everything worked fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance from the University which send me mails about things I needed to have in mind before entering the country and practical things I needed to do in the beginning of living in Japan, like for example getting a citizen card and enrolling in their health system. The dormitory – run by the university – was also very helpful if I had any questions about living in Japan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at a dorm very close to the university campus which was run by the university. Nishi Waseda/Takadanobaba is a very nice area and I totally recommend it. It was very easy to get, I just applied through a platform/survey and a month after I got a room at the dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The rules for living at dorm in Japan is very strict. I was not allowed to have any visitors, you are told to be quite and alcohol is forbidden in the shared areas of the dormitory. The dormitory make some social gatherings through the semester where they provide pizza, snacks and soft drinks but the events stops around 20-21 o clock because they are afraid of noise complains from the neighbors. Living at a dorm in Japan is very different from living at a dorm in Denmark. However, it is a good place to meet other students from the university and I got some really good friends from the dorm. I also heard that other dorms where less strict.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university is very conservative and may parents had to sign different documents despite I am in my late 20's. The registration process is very straight forward however you must send in a lot of documents which takes a lot of time. On the other hand, you get to experience a very interesting and beautiful country and it was totally worth all the paperwork.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You parents have to sign a lot of documents, you have to make a document explaining why you want to study at Waseda University and find a personal supervisor (this takes some time). Moreover, you have to prove that you financially can live in Tokyo (the SU-office will create a document for you). There is a lot of other documents, but I can't remember them all. Everything about the registration process is explained on the university's webpage.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an office at Waseda University for international students where you can ask questions by email or phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The course registration is very easy. It is very similar to the one on KU-net. I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you register for courses outside of your faculty on Waseda University, you cannot cancel them. I took four courses (8 credits=30 ECTS) and I think this was the perfect number of courses where I felt academically involved but also had time to explore Tokyo and go travel.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is relatively easy. If I had to go on exchange again, I would find a University where the academic level is more challenging. On the other hand, it was very interesting to learn about International Politics and Immigration Politics through the lenses of Japanese lecturers. The university is also famous for its journalism courses, so it was interesting to learn about the differences in Japanese and western story telling and newsflow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The format of the lectures is like high school/gymnasiet where you are between 25-10 students per course and the teacher knows your name. That way I became more engaged in the lectures and readings compared to the more the more anonymous lecture format in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
-	Causal Inference in Social Science A (Basic)
-	Theory of International Politics (E)
-	Refugee and Migration Studies and Contemporary Issues
-	Contemporary Journalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Theory of ‘International Politics' and ‘Refugee and Migration Studies and Contemporary Issues' is mainly based on western theory, however the empirical cases we discussed was related to Japan which was interesting. Contemporary Journalism was also interesting because you learned about how news are created and you also learned about cultural differences in news making.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying things for your room like pillows and towels.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in the supermarket is very expensive, but eating out is very cheap. You can get a super great meal at a very cozy restaurant for 60-100 DKK. Because the dormitory kitchen was very minimalistic and the food is amazing in Japan I decided to eat out a lot. That part you have to look forward to!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Tokyo is a city with an infinity of possibilities which I loved! They have some great museums, architecture, public bath (which is one of my favorite things) and other cultural things. They have the concept called izakaya which I can recommend a lot. It is a restaurant where you share small tapas plates of Japanese food and drink beer, sake, plum wine, soft drinks or what you prefer. I started at a karate club at Waseda University which was fun and a good way to meet other students. Many did not speak English but it was still ok easy to communicate because it is about sport.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University provides many opportunities to engage in social activities: There are traveling clubs, different sport clubs you can join and there is also different cultural thing like a tea ceremony club or painting club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Karate is a lot of fun and you dont need to have any experience beforehand.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to travel because the public transportation system is so good. Lots of museums, beautiful Japanese gardens and hiking trips. You feel very safe when traveling and there is often someone who would like to help you.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general people at Waseda University are very nice, however, some students are very conservative at the university and I found that very challenging. My dorm neighbor for example said things like “poor people are lazy people” or “women who give birth should not get any social support from the government because giving birth is like being on vacation” and another dorm neighbor used words like 'nazi-feminists' and showed me a blackface joke on YouTube. I also had one lecturer saying some racist things so I dropped the course.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in a club or some of the activities made on whatsapp groups for exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That some students and professors had very different political believes than I and said some very conservative things. I found that very overwhelming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very polite and helpful in general. Japan has a very rich culture regarding art, handcraft, tea culture and architecture which I found very inspiring. I also find the approach towards nature inspiring too. Trash on the streets and in the nature is little, the tap-water in Tokyo taste good, they have a lot of parks and green areas, good public transportation, and it in general feel like many cares a lot about nature and environmental issues in Japan.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look forward to all the amazing things you didn't know that you needed in life, like public bath/onzen, izakaya and jazz cafes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most of the exchange students are around 18-24 years old.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a new way of living. Being on exchange feels like living in a bobble where you constantly experience new things and get new experiences. I definitely recommend going on exchange and Tokyo is a beautiful city to live in.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That some students have very different political beliefs from what I have experienced in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
